name: Braised Veal
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: piece of the shoulder weighing about five pounds
ingredients.originalText: A piece of the shoulder weighing about five pounds

ingredients.name: piece of butter the size of half an egg
ingredients.originalText: A piece of butter the size of half an egg

ingredients.name: About two tablespoonfuls of hot water
ingredients.originalText: About two tablespoonfuls of hot water

instructions.text: Have the bone removed and tie up the meat to make it firm
Put a piece of butter the size of half an egg, together with a few shavings of onion, into a kettle or stone crock and let it get hot
Salt and pepper the veal and put it into the kettle, cover it tightly and put it over a medium fire until the meat is brown on both sides, turning it occasionally
Set the kettle back on the stove, where it will simmer slowly for about two hours and a half
Before setting the meat back on the stove, see if the juice of the meat together with the butter do not make gravy enough, and if not, put in about two tablespoonfuls of hot water
When the gravy is cold it will be like jelly
It can be served hot with the hot meat, or cold with the cold meat

source.originalInstructions:
1. Have the bone removed and tie up the meat to make it firm
2. Put a piece of butter the size of half an egg, together with a few shavings of onion, into a kettle or stone crock and let it get hot
3. Salt and pepper the veal and put it into the kettle, cover it tightly and put it over a medium fire until the meat is brown on both sides, turning it occasionally
4. Set the kettle back on the stove, where it will simmer slowly for about two hours and a half
5. Before setting the meat back on the stove, see if the juice of the meat together with the butter do not make gravy enough, and if not, put in about two tablespoonfuls of hot water
6. When the gravy is cold it will be like jelly
7. It can be served hot with the hot meat, or cold with the cold meat
